resources.string: Dynamic colors follow your wallpaper on Android 12+.
How often live metrics refresh while a screen is visible. Longer intervals use less battery. Nothing is polled in the background.
Graphs are kept on this device only while you use the Monitor screen. Up to 2000 samples per metric.

Internet: only for the network diagnostics you start yourself (ping, DNS). Network state: to tell whether Wi-Fi or mobile data is available, and to run a test over the one you pick. In Local mode FrameX opens no connection. Installed apps list: to find games and apps you may choose to stop; it never leaves your phone. Stop background processes: only for apps you confirm. Draw over other apps: only for the FPS overlay. Change system settings: only to dim the screen during a game. Wake lock: only the Wi-Fi low-latency lock during a game. FrameX reads no personal files.
When on, the Play button in Games checks temperature, memory, battery saver and refresh rate, then picks the profile. When off, it applies the game\'s own saved profile.

A small draggable box over your game, no root needed, with FPS and battery temperature. FPS is measured exactly when Shizuku or wireless debugging is connected; otherwise it shows n/a unless you turn on the screen-capture estimate below. It appears while a game from your list is running.

Off by default. When on and neither Shizuku nor wireless debugging is connected, Play asks to capture the screen so FrameX can count how often the picture changes (an estimate, about ±2 FPS, marked ~). Nothing is recorded or saved. You are asked every time.
Needs the permission to draw over other apps.
Where FrameX may use the internet. Only the network tests you start yourself use it; nothing runs in the background.
FrameX makes no internet connection at all (the optional wireless-debugging link goes only to your own phone). Monitoring, optimization, games, FPS and benchmarks all work offline.
Network tests can run over the connections you allow. You choose Wi-Fi or mobile data (or both, to compare) for every test.

When on, Play and Quick Boost stop the apps you used in the last 24 hours by themselves, before the game opens, and show what was stopped. System apps, the keyboard, launcher, dialer, SMS and anything on your never-stop list are skipped. Stopped apps may restart later; unsaved data in them can be lost.
Method now: real force-stop with shell access (Shizuku or wireless debugging), each app checked afterwards.
Method now: real force-stop through the accessibility service, each app checked afterwards.
Method now: background kill. Android does not confirm it per app and it does not touch apps with running services.

For a real force-stop without Shizuku, turn on the \"FrameX boost\" accessibility service. It only presses \"Force stop\" in the Settings app info page while a boost runs. On Android 13+ you may first need App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings.
Ticked apps are skipped by every automatic boost.

This build has no accessibility helper, so Google Play Protect does not block it. Shizuku or wireless debugging still give a real force-stop. A separate \"boost\" build with the accessibility helper exists for people who want it.

Gives FrameX the same shell access Shizuku gives: game mode, battery saver, real FPS and real force-stop. FrameX connects only to your own phone, never to the internet. Pairing is needed once; reconnecting later is one tap.

1) Settings → About phone → tap the build number 7 times. 2) Developer options → turn on Wireless debugging (the phone must be on Wi-Fi). 3) Press Pair here: FrameX opens Developer options and posts a notification. 4) Open Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. 5) Pull the notification down and type the 6-digit code there. 6) Press Connect. 7) For mobile data only: press \"Keep working without Wi-Fi\" once, then you can leave Wi-Fi.
If Connect finds nothing, type the port shown under \"IP address & Port\" on the Wireless debugging screen.

Wireless debugging needs Wi-Fi. Press the button below once while connected: FrameX switches ADB to plain TCP (the same as \"adb tcpip 5555\"), so it keeps working on mobile data after you leave Wi-Fi. Android will ask \"Allow USB debugging?\" for FrameX: tick \"Always allow\" and accept. Also turn on USB debugging in Developer options. It resets when the phone restarts. While it is on, port 5555 accepts connections only from devices you approve.
TCP mode is on: this works without Wi-Fi until the phone restarts. After a restart you need Wi-Fi once more (it can be a network without internet).
Accept the \"Allow USB debugging?\" dialog for FrameX (tick \"Always allow\"). You have about a minute.
Not showing: allow drawing over other apps first.
Not showing: FrameX needs Usage access to see which app is open (Games screen).
The detection service is running. The overlay appears in the apps chosen above.
The detection service is not running, so no overlay can appear. Android may have stopped it.

If the overlay disappears after a while, the phone is probably stopping FrameX in the background. On HyperOS open the app info and set Battery saver to \"No restrictions\", turn on Autostart, and lock FrameX in the recent apps.
